name: Knight Relay
description: A fictional doubles chess invitational at East Hall.

slides.title: KNIGHT RELAY
items: EAST HALL INVITATIONAL
Doubles chess. Partners switch every fifth move.

slides.title: THE FIFTH MOVE
items: The opening player chooses the first five moves for their side. Their partner watches from behind the table and keeps the score sheet.
After move five, the seated player starts the opposing clock. Partners exchange seats in silence. The new player inherits the position and the remaining time.

slides.title: ROOM FOR TWO
items: On either side of the board, one chair faces the table and one waits behind it. The aisle stays clear so partners can change places without interrupting the next game.
Spectators follow the demonstration board from the end of the hall. Only the floor arbiter enters the playing aisle during a round.

slides.title: READ THE ROUTE
items: A warm-up for the handover. With the other pieces removed, a knight on d4 can reach e7 in two moves through f5. The three marks follow that route from bottom to top.
The first player names the destination. Their partner names the intermediate square, then plays both jumps on the practice board.

slides.title: ONE CLOCK
items: 18 minutes
Each pair starts with eighteen minutes for the entire game. The clock keeps running through every exchange of seats. There is no increment.
The arbiter checks both displays before the first move. If either partner notices a clock fault, they pause both sides and call the arbiter.

slides.title: SATURDAY DRAW
items: Opening round
Pairs draw a table at check-in. The lower draw number takes White in the first game.
Second round
Partners reverse the opening seat. Pairings go up beside the hall doors after results are checked.
Final round
The leading pairs meet at the front tables. Spectators can follow the live position from the gallery.

slides.title: THE SILENT SEAT
items: “I could see the fork from behind the chair. By the time I sat down, the board had changed.”
Mara Ellis, player in the rehearsal match
The silent partner records moves throughout the game. That gives both players a common record when they replay the position after the round.

slides.title: COUNT THE POINTS
items: A win adds one point to the pair’s total, whichever partner plays the final move.
½
A draw earns half a point for each pair. Both players initial the same result slip.
A loss earns zero. If the final totals tie, the event compares the combined scores of each pair’s opponents.

slides.title: THE RESULT SLIP
items: Table 04
White   /   Ellis & Fox
Black   /   Chan & Bell
½ – ½
After the players agreed a draw, both pairs checked the board number and the colour assignment. The arbiter carried the signed slip to the results desk.

slides.title: FOUR TABLES
items: 4 boards · 4 clocks · 16 chairs
Four games can run at once. Each table seats two active players, with one waiting chair behind each side. An extra clock stays at the arbiter’s desk.
The demonstration board belongs at the end of the hall. Spectators can gather there while players keep a clear route back to their seats.

slides.title: BACK TO THE BOARD
items: After the round
The pair resets the pieces to its first handover. The outgoing player describes the plan they had in mind. The incoming player shows the move they considered first.
The score sheet settles the move order. Each pair circles one position to replay at the open boards before the next round.

slides.title: AT THE LAST BELL
items: Bring the signed score sheet to the arbiter. The team at the results desk checks it against the table slip before posting the final standings.
The winning pair replays one handover position on the demonstration board. Both players explain what they saw from the second chair.
